content.doc_md:
## Tutorials

The ADDDATE() function adds a time/date interval to a date and then returns the date.

OR:

### Code Examples

```
SELECT ADDDATE("2017-06-15", INTERVAL 10 DAY);

---

ADDDATE(
date
, INTERVAL
value addunit
)

---

ADDDATE(
date
,
days
)

---

SELECT ADDDATE("2017-06-15 09:34:21", INTERVAL 15 MINUTE);

---

SELECT ADDDATE("2017-06-15 09:34:21", INTERVAL -3 HOUR);

---

SELECT ADDDATE("2017-06-15", INTERVAL -2 MONTH);
```

## Tutorials

The ADDTIME() function adds a time interval to a time/datetime and then returns the time/datetime.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT ADDTIME("2017-06-15 
  09:34:21", "2");

---

ADDTIME(
datetime
,
addtime
)

---

SELECT ADDTIME("2017-06-15 
  09:34:21.000001", "5.000003");

---

SELECT ADDTIME("2017-06-15 09:34:21.000001", "2:10:5.000003");

---

SELECT ADDTIME("2017-06-15 
  09:34:21.000001", "5 2:10:5.000003");

---

SELECT ADDTIME("09:34:21.000001", "2:10:5.000003");
```

## Tutorials

The CURDATE() function returns the current date.

Note:The date is returned as 
"YYYY-MM-DD" (string) or as YYYYMMDD (numeric).

Note:This function equals theCURRENT_DATE()function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT CURDATE();

---

CURDATE()

---

SELECT CURDATE() + 1;
```

## Tutorials

The CURRENT_DATE() function returns the current date.

Note:The date is returned as 
"YYYY-MM-DD" (string) or as YYYYMMDD (numeric).

Note:This function equals theCURDATE()function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT CURRENT_DATE();

---

CURRENT_DATE()

---

SELECT CURRENT_DATE() + 1;
```

## Tutorials

The CURRENT_TIME() function returns the current time.

Note:The time is returned as 
"HH-MM-SS" (string) or as HHMMSS.uuuuuu (numeric).

Note:This function equals theCURTIME()function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT CURRENT_TIME();

---

CURRENT_TIME()

---

SELECT CURRENT_TIME() + 1;
```
